Netflix is testing AI Discover, a new tab on its TV app that suggests what to watch based on your mood.
You pick a theme like "Scare Me" or "Quick Watches" and narrow it down from there.
It starts with a limited group of US members watching in English on supported TVs.

slides.heading: Meet *AI Discover*
paras: Netflix is rolling out AI Discover, a new tab on its TV app that suggests titles based on what you are in the mood for.
Netflix calls it a "test kitchen" for trying new ways to find something to watch.

slides.heading: Pick a *mood*, not a title
paras: You choose a theme like "Something Light," "Scare Me," "Family Movie Night" or "Quick Watches," each previewed with a clip.
Smaller themes narrow the list, and "Something Different" starts fresh.

slides.heading: Tell it *"not this one"*
paras: A "Tune Your Recommendations" button next to Play lets you save a title or ask Netflix to stop suggesting it.

paras.t: For now it is a limited US test on TVs, in English, with more members added in the coming weeks.

slides.hook: Your TV is starting to choose for you. Follow to see where Netflix takes AI Discover next.

paragraphs.text: Netflix has started testing AI Discover, a new tab in its TV app that recommends shows and movies based on what a member is in the mood for. The company announced the feature on November 3, 2026, and described the tab as its "test kitchen," a place to try new approaches to discovery before deciding which ones to keep, according to TechCrunch.

The rollout begins in the United States with a limited group of members who use Netflix in English on supported TVs. Netflix plans to add more members over the coming weeks, but has not said how many people are included in the first group, What's on Netflix reported.

Members who have the feature see a Discover button, marked with a red gem icon and a "New" label, in the top navigation bar of the TV app. Inside, they choose from a set of themes, each previewed with a clip from a show or movie. The themes reflect a mood, the people watching, the time available, or what is new and trending. Examples include "Something Light," "Scare Me," "Family Movie Night" and "Quick Watches."

Picking a theme opens a page of matching titles. Below the results, more specific themes let members narrow the list further, and a "Something Different" option brings up a fresh set. Netflix says the feature runs on a new intelligence layer that responds to member input in real time and keeps learning, and What's on Netflix noted that recommendations are generated live, so results can differ from one visit to the next.

Each title also gets a "Tune Your Recommendations" button next to the Play and My List buttons. Members can use it to keep a title they like or to tell Netflix they are not interested or have already seen it, and titles removed this way are not suggested again inside AI Discover.

The first version has no chat box or typing. Netflix pointed to the difficulty of typing on a TV, What's on Netflix reported, and said it is working on voice and natural language search, though nothing has been announced for TVs. Members cannot sign up for the test or remove the tab if they are in it, and only standard profiles have access, not kids profiles.

Netflix has not shared plans for mobile apps, other languages or other countries. The company said a Help Center page listing compatible TVs is planned, that choices made in AI Discover do not influence its content decisions, and that it expects more experiments in the new year, possibly including tests built around story elements of favorite titles.
Member use and feedback will decide which experiments stay in AI Discover, which are improved, and which may move into the main Netflix experience, according to TechCrunch and Unite.AI.

The design avoids the chatbot approach that many AI products use. By keeping the input to themes and buttons on a remote, Netflix is testing whether AI can cut the time spent scrolling without asking viewers to change how they use a TV. Calling the tab a test kitchen also gives the company room to drop ideas that do not work.

The next signal is the Help Center list of compatible TVs and how quickly Netflix widens the test beyond the first group of US members, along with any move of AI Discover features into the main home screen.
